findings.title: pre-send marker (send_attempt_started) is non-atomically cleared: crash or clear-failure between deliver-throw and clearSessionDeliveryRecoveryState leaves a never-sent entry that next recovery permanently fails (over-refusal / state resurrection)
findings.body: drainQueuedEntry writes recoveryState="send_attempt_started" BEFORE deliver() (line 160). On a genuine pre-send failure (deliver throws before reaching the platform - the common busy/transient case in drainRestartContinuationQueue, which loops this drain live up to RESTART_CONTINUATION_BUSY_MAX_ATTEMPTS), the intended recovery is line 186 clearSessionDeliveryRecoveryState + line 187 failSessionDelivery (retry preserved). But that clear is a SEPARATE upsert from the deliver attempt and from failSessionDelivery. If the process crashes between deliver throwing (161) and the clear committing (186), OR if clearSessionDeliveryRecoveryState itself throws (caught at 189, swallowed as "failed"), the durable state is left at send_attempt_started for a message that was NEVER sent. On the NEXT recovery the early-refuse branch (lines 144-151) treats send_attempt_started IDENTICALLY to unknown_after_send and unconditionally moveToFailed. A delivery that never reached the platform is silently dropped to failed/ with no replay. The outbound queue tolerates an identical refuse only because it has reconcileUnknownSend to recover the truth; the session queue has NO reconcile capability (chosen_fix=0 explicitly defers it), so this is a permanent message loss, not a deferred decision. This widens the documented at-least-once tradeoff from 'sent-but-unacked' (acceptable) to 'never-sent-but-marker-stuck' (message loss). The marker is overloaded: send_attempt_started means both 'maybe never sent' and (transiently, between deliver success at 161 and the upgrade at 164) 'already sent'. Recovery resolves the ambiguity by always refusing, which is safe for wrong-output but unsafe for delivery-loss on the pre-send arm.
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish the two marker states at recovery. send_attempt_started (pre-send, possibly never sent) should NOT be unconditionally moved to failed/: either (a) treat a recovered send_attempt_started as replay-eligible bounded by retryCount/maxRetries (accepting at-most a duplicate on the narrow sent-then-crash-before-upgrade window, matching design doc's 'duplicate visible message only when explicitly disclosed'), or (b) keep refusing only unknown_after_send and refuse send_attempt_started only after it has survived one recovery pass (promote-then-refuse). Minimum: do not collapse the two states into one refuse branch at lines 144-147. Alternatively make the pre-send clear+fail atomic with the deliver-attempt bookkeeping (single upsert) so a crash cannot strand send_attempt_started.
findings.regression_test: Enqueue an agentTurn. PASS 1: deliver throws a transient error (pre-send, e.g. 'busy'), AND spy clearSessionDeliveryRecoveryState to throw once (models clear-failure / crash-before-clear) so the durable recoveryState stays send_attempt_started. PASS 2: re-enter recovery with a deliver that would succeed. Without fix: entry is moved to failed/ and deliver is NOT called again (deliverCount stays 0, message lost) -> RED on expect(deliverCount).toBe(1). With fix: send_attempt_started is replayed -> deliverCount===1.

findings.title: happy-path double-write: markSessionDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown (post-send) and ackSessionDelivery are separate upserts/deletes; the second-write (upgrade to unknown_after_send) is redundant work that only narrows, never closes, the divergence window and adds an extra crash point on every successful recovery
findings.body: After deliver() succeeds (line 162 delivered=true), the code does THREE more durable ops in sequence: line 164 markSessionDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown (upsert recoveryState=unknown_after_send), then line 165 ackSessionDelivery (delete row). For in-process crash safety the unknown_after_send upgrade at 164 is unnecessary: a crash between 161-success and 165-ack already leaves recoveryState=send_attempt_started, which recovery refuses anyway (per the early-refuse branch). So line 164 adds an extra SQLite write and an extra crash window on EVERY successful recovery without changing the recovery decision (both markers refuse). It is justified only if an external reconcile (full-adapter-reconcile candidate) later needs to distinguish them - but chosen_fix=0 has no reconcile, so under this PR the distinction is dead. The risk it introduces: if markSessionDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown throws (caught at 168), delivered=true correctly forces moveToFailed (line 176), so no replay - safe. Net: not a correctness defect under chosen_fix=0, but it is extra divergence surface and contradicts the SOL's own note that the typed-error/extra-state mechanism is 'dead' here. Worth dropping line 164 to match the actual recovery contract, or documenting why the post-send upgrade is retained for the future reconcile path.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the markSessionDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown upgrade at line 164 (since send_attempt_started already triggers refuse, the upgrade changes no decision under chosen_fix=0) and rely solely on the durable send_attempt_started + in-process delivered flag; OR add an explicit comment that unknown_after_send is persisted only to feed the future full-adapter-reconcile candidate, and confirm a test asserts recovery treats the two markers identically today.
findings.regression_test: Enqueue an agentTurn. deliver succeeds; spy ackSessionDelivery to throw once AND assert the durable row after PASS 1 carries recoveryState===send_attempt_started even when markSessionDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown is ALSO spied to throw - then PASS 2 must still refuse (deliverCount===1). Demonstrates the unknown_after_send upgrade is not load-bearing for the refuse decision.
